releases.name: TeleMeetBot v1.3.2
releases.body:
# TeleMeetBot v1.3.2 Release Notes

TeleMeetBot v1.3.2 introduces **Persistent Media Playlist Queues with Previous/Next controls** and a comprehensive overhaul of **Google Meet Admission & Session Reliability**.

## 1. Persistent Media Playlist Queue & Telegram Staging

- **50-Item Batch Submission**: Users can forward multiple Telegram audio/video messages in batch, or paste up to 50 URLs (YouTube, MP4, MP3, web streams) separated by newlines in a single message.
- **Playback Controls**: Added interactive **⏮ Previous** and **⏭ Next** inline buttons to the session card alongside Pause/Resume, Restart, and Stop.
- **Queue Management**: Inspect active playlists with track positions (e.g., `📋 Playlist: 3 / 50`), upcoming items, direct track jumping, item removal, or clear queue with confirmation.
- **Auto-Advance with Ended Detection**: Automatically advances to the next playlist item upon completion, checking both HTML5 media `ended` events and YouTube IFrame Player API `getPlayerState() === 0`.
- **Media Lease Protection**: Queued local media files are locked under `queue:<sessionID>` leases, preventing premature reclamation by background janitor sweeps.
- **SQLite Persistence**: Playlist order and current track index persist across session restarts.

## 2. Google Meet Admission & Lifecycle Reliability

- **Explicit Observable State Machine**:
  `QUEUED → STARTING → JOINING → WAITING_FOR_ADMISSION → ADMITTED → ACTIVE → LEAVING → COMPLETED`
  with distinct terminal outcomes: `FAILED`, `CANCELLED`, and `TIMED_OUT`.
- **Single-Flight Meeting Deduplication**: Prevents duplicate sessions or workers targeting the same Google Meet room (`Shortcode(meetURL)` matching), avoiding browser knock conflicts and rate limits.
- **Debounced Join Requests**: Prevents hammering or cancelling in-flight "Ask to join" requests by debouncing join clicks and verifying button enablement.
- **Modern Web Framework Input Synchronization**: Uses native property descriptor setters (`HTMLInputElement.prototype.value`) so Google Meet's Angular/React/Lit form validation recognizes guest names and activates the join button.
- **Jittered Bounded Backoff**: For host-restricted meetings ("No one can join a meeting unless invited or admitted by the host"), re-request entry cycles back off with randomized jitter (20s–30s + jitter) instead of rigid 30s reloads, eliminating poll storms and reducing delays when hosts arrive.
- **Actionable Host Admission Timeouts**: Returns clear guidance when a meeting host fails to admit the guest within `admit_wait_seconds`.

## Verification & Tests

- Full race-detector suite passed clean (`go test -race ./...`).
- Regression tests for 50-item sequential queue, boundaries, lease management, concurrency, admission state transitions, single-flight deduplication, and reload jitter.

releases.name: TeleMeetBot v1.3.1
releases.body:
# TeleMeetBot v1.3.1 — long videos no longer die mid-playback

**A patch release with one headline fix: a downloaded file could be deleted
while a session was still streaming it.** Anything longer than the one-hour
download TTL — a long YouTube download, a paused stream, a talk left running —
died mid-playback with a playback error and, in download mode, an aborted
session.

## The bug

Downloaded media carried a hard one-hour TTL, and that TTL was enforced as a
playback deadline rather than as a cleanup policy:

- The media janitor (`Sweep`) deleted **any** expired entry, without checking
  whether a session was still streaming it. A two-hour video downloaded at
  noon was unlinked at 13:00, mid-playback.
- The session watchdog treated the same deadline as a session-level failure:
  when `ExpiresAt` passed, `watch()` errored the session out instead of
  letting playback continue.
- The file server then served a path that no longer existed, so seeks, range
  requests and resumed playback all failed with a hard error.

The TTL is the right policy for *cleaning up abandoned files*. It was the wrong
policy for *media in use*.

## The fix: active-media leases

Downloaded files are now pinned to the session that owns them for the entire
lifetime of that session. The TTL is unchanged at one hour, but it is now an
**orphan-reclamation policy** instead of a hard cut-off:

- `media.Manager` gains a lease API (`Lease`, `Release`,
  `ReleaseAndDelete`, `LeaseOwners`). A session leases its file the moment it
  adopts it, before the file is recorded as the session's local media — so
  there is no window in which the janitor can delete a file the session is
  about to play.
- The janitor skips any expired entry that a lease holds, and logs that it
  retained it. Playback continues for as long as the owning session is alive,
  regardless of video duration, elapsed time or paused playback.
- Releasing a lease reclaims the file: `Release` deletes an expired, unowned
  entry at once, while a file that is still fresh is left for the janitor and
  its own deadline. `ReleaseAndDelete` is the teardown path (stop, close,
  cleanup, mode change): it deletes immediately unless another session still
  holds the same entry — for example two sessions sharing one Telegram file.
- `Remove()` stays the unconditional admin path and always wins over a lease.
- Leases are **in-memory only**. A process restart drops every pin, so stale
  leases can never protect orphaned files: crash recovery and the startup
  sweep behave exactly as before, and disk protection (download size cap,
  timeout, concurrency, path validation, SSRF defences, minimum free disk) is
  untouched.

The session watchdog no longer fails a session at `ExpiresAt`. It logs once
that the file is past its TTL and held by an active lease, and playback
continues.

## Configuration

No key was added, removed or renamed; every v1.3.0 config loads unchanged.
The semantics of one key are clarified in the docs:

```yaml
download:
  ttl_minutes: 60   # orphan cleanup: reclaims files no session is streaming;
                    # an active session keeps its file for its whole lifetime
```

`Status` gains one read-only field, `leased_files`, reporting how many managed
files are currently held by an active session.

## Regression tests

Existing tests that required an active file to expire were rewritten, and new
deterministic tests added (short TTLs and an injectable clock — no test waits
an actual hour). Proven by the suite:

- an active download remains accessible **after** its original one-hour
  deadline, under repeated janitor sweeps;
- playback requests, including HTTP range requests, do not fail because the
  janitor deleted the file;
- stopping a session or switching media releases the old file promptly, while
  the new media is leased before it is adopted;
- inactive expired files are still reclaimed;
- restart recovery, concurrent cleanup, failed downloads and multi-session
  ownership remain safe.

Full suite, race detector and `go vet` are green.

## Artifacts

Native binaries for Linux (amd64, arm64, arm v6/v7, 386), macOS (Intel, Apple
Silicon) and Windows (amd64, arm64), plus `SHA256SUMS` and the installers:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/Opselon/TeleMeetBot-TeleMeetBot-implementation/releases/download/v1.3.1/install.sh | sh -s -- --version v1.3.1
```

Docker image published as
`ghcr.io/opselon/telemeetbot-telemeetbot-implementation:v1.3.1` (and `:latest`),
multi-arch for `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`.

releases.name: TeleMeetBot v1.3.0
releases.body:
# TeleMeetBot v1.3.0 — the one-command install actually works

**A patch release with one headline fix: the published one-command installer was
broken on every Debian, Ubuntu and Alpine host.** Everything else is hardening
that makes that class of failure impossible to ship again.

## The bug

The v1.2.0 install script used bash-only syntax (`[[ ]]`, `${var//x/y}`), but
the documented one-command install pipes it straight into `sh`:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/Opselon/TeleMeetBot-TeleMeetBot-implementation/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh
```

On Debian and Ubuntu `/bin/sh` is **dash**; on Alpine it is **busybox**. Neither
implements `[[`, so the script died before installing anything:

```
sh: 36: [[: not found
sh: 80: [[: not found
error: resolved version 'latest' does not look like a tag (vX.Y.Z); refusing to install
```

The failure was silent in two ways: the process usually exited 0 (so `curl | sh`
looked successful to a caller not watching stderr), and CI never caught it
because every CI step invoked the script with `bash` — a different interpreter
than the one the README tells users to use.

## The fix

`scripts/install.sh` is rewritten in POSIX `sh` and carries a `shellcheck -s sh`
gate. Verified under **dash**, **busybox** and **bash**, and in clean
minimal-container environments (Debian `bookworm-slim` and Alpine) with no
build toolchain installed.

Nothing about the flag surface or the install layout changed:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/Opselon/TeleMeetBot-TeleMeetBot-implementation/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh
```

## Hardening in this release

- **Post-install version verification.** The installer now runs the binary it
  just installed and matches its `--version` against the release tag. A corrupt
  download, a truncated archive, or a version-stamping mistake in the build
  aborts the install instead of being reported as success.
- **CI now tests the published invocation.** The installer smoke job pipes the
  script through `sh` (with `curl | sh`, exactly as documented) instead of
  running it under `bash`, and asserts `dash -n` plus `shellcheck -s sh`.
- **Version-mismatch regression test.** A new CI case serves an archive whose
  binary reports a different version than the requested tag and requires the
  installer to refuse it.
- **Release smokeJobs assert the stamped version.** Every release binary's
  `--version` must contain the release tag, so the installer's new version gate
  can never be defeated by broken `ldflags` wiring.
- **Post-publish install verification.** The release workflow now runs the
  published installer against the release it just published — downloading the
  real `install.sh` from the release assets and installing into a sandbox — so
  a release cannot be announced as working without a user-side install
  succeeding.
- **Documentation fixes.** The website install guides pointed at the stale
  `raw.githubusercontent.com/…/main/scripts/install.sh` bootstrap URL (an
  unpinned, branch-following URL that bypasses checksum verification); they now
  use the release asset. The README pin examples were updated from v1.1.0 to
  v1.2.0.

## Upgrading from v1.2.0

```bash
# re-run the one-command install against the new release
curl -fsSL https://github.com/Opselon/TeleMeetBot-TeleMeetBot-implementation/releases/download/v1.3.0/install.sh | sh -s -- --version v1.3.0
```

Or, if you installed with a custom prefix:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/Opselon/TeleMeetBot-TeleMeetBot-implementation/releases/download/v1.3.0/install.sh \
  | sh -s -- --version v1.3.0 --prefix /your/prefix --config-dir /your/config
```

The install is idempotent: re-running over an existing install replaces the
binary and leaves the config, data directory and service registration
untouched. No configuration key was removed or renamed; every v1.2.0 config
loads unchanged.

If you installed v1.0.0/v1.1.0 with the old `raw.githubusercontent.com`
bootstrapping URL, switch to the pinned release URL above — the branch URL
serves whatever is on `main` today and validates nothing.

## Artifacts

Native binaries for Linux (amd64, arm64, arm v6/v7, 386), macOS (Intel, Apple
Silicon) and Windows (amd64, arm64), plus `SHA256SUMS` and the installers
themselves:

```bash
curl -fsSLO https://github.com/Opselon/TeleMeetBot-TeleMeetBot-implementation/releases/download/v1.3.0/SHA256SUMS
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing
```

Docker image published as
`ghcr.io/opselon/telemeetbot-telemeetbot-implementation:v1.3.0` (and `:latest`),
multi-arch for `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`.

releases.name: TeleMeetBot v1.2.0
releases.body:
# TeleMeetBot v1.2.0 — one command, every platform

**The install release: a verified one-command installer for Windows, Linux and macOS, a setup
wizard that works everywhere, and the safe lifecycle (upgrade, backup, rollback, uninstall)
around it.**

Minor bump over v1.1.0: no configuration key was removed or renamed, and every existing config
continues to load. The install surface is new; the engine, bot and website are unchanged.

## Install in one command

**Linux / macOS:**

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/Opselon/TeleMeetBot-TeleMeetBot-implementation/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh
```

**Windows (PowerShell 5.1+):**

```powershell
irm https://github.com/Opselon/TeleMeetBot-TeleMeetBot-implementation/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex
```

**Docker:**

```bash
docker compose run --rm telemeetbot telemeetbot --wizard --config /data/telemeetbot.yml
docker compose up -d
```

Each installer:

1. detects the OS and CPU architecture (`amd64` / `arm64` / `armv6` / `armv7` / `386`),
   dependencies, permissions and whether it is running elevated;
2. resolves the latest **release tag** and refuses anything that does not look like one;
3. downloads the matching archive and **verifies it against the release's published SHA-256
   checksums** — a tampered or corrupted archive aborts the install before anything is written;
4. installs the binary (`/usr/local/bin/telemeetbot`, `$env:ProgramFiles\TeleMeetBot`, or a
   per-user fallback when not elevated);
5. stages a fail-closed template config — an existing config is **never** overwritten;
6. installs the OS service: systemd unit on Linux, a Windows service through the SCM, a launchd
   agent on macOS;
7. runs the interactive setup wizard, then verifies the health endpoint.

Pin a specific release for unattended installs:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/Opselon/TeleMeetBot-TeleMeetBot-implementation/releases/download/v1.2.0/install.sh | sh -s -- --version v1.2.0
```

Verify an archive yourself before installing:

```bash
curl -fsSLO https://github.com/Opselon/TeleMeetBot-TeleMeetBot-implementation/releases/download/v1.2.0/SHA256SUMS
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing
```

## Native binaries for every supported platform

Built and smoke-tested on real runners, not just cross-compiled:

| Platform | Archive |
| --- | --- |
| Linux amd64 / arm64 / armv6 / armv7 / 386 | `telemeetbot-linux-*.tar.gz` |
| macOS amd64 (Intel) / arm64 (Apple Silicon) | `telemeetbot-darwin-*.tar.gz` |
| Windows amd64 / arm64 | `telemeetbot-windows-*.zip` |

One `SHA256SUMS` manifest covers every archive in the release. The multi-arch Docker image is
published as `ghcr.io/opselon/telemeetbot-telemeetbot-implementation:v1.2.0` (and `:latest`).

## Setup wizard

- One Chromium question per platform: `apt-get` on Debian/Ubuntu, Homebrew on macOS, `winget` on
  Windows. Platforms without a supported package manager print a manual hint instead of running a
  wrong command.
- One service question per platform through the new `internal/svcinst` package: a hardened
  systemd unit (`NoNewPrivileges`, `ProtectSystem=full`, `PrivateTmp`), a Windows service with a
  restart-on-failure policy, a launchd agent with `KeepAlive`.
- **Re-running the wizard over a live install is safe**: the previous config is backed up to
  `config.yml.bak` before the new one is written.

## Lifecycle

```bash
telemeetbot --wizard                  # re-run setup (backs up the previous config)
telemeetbot --restore-backup          # roll the config back to that backup
telemeetbot --check                   # doctor: config, browser, permissions, disk, network
telemeetbot --uninstall               # stop + remove the service, then the binary
telemeetbot --uninstall --keep-binary # remove only the service registration
```

- **`--uninstall` never deletes the config, the data directory or the session history** — the
  bot token and saved meetings survive an uninstall so a re-install picks up where you left off.
- Uninstalling a **running** service requires `--yes` or a typed `yes`; without confirmation it
  fails closed and leaves the bot alone.
- The uninstall refuses to delete a binary that sits in a source checkout (a developer build),
  and converges when run twice.

## Windows service support

The binary now runs natively under the Windows Service Control Manager: it auto-detects when it
was started by the SCM, runs the bot in the service loop, reports state transitions and honours
the 30-second Stop window with a clean shutdown. Signal handling was split per platform because
SIGTERM cannot be caught on Windows. Health, disk-space and media-manager code that used
`statfs(2)` now goes through a per-platform disk layer, so the whole tree builds and runs on
Windows and macOS.

## Upgrading from v1.1.0

- Replace the binary; the config format is unchanged. The installer does this without touching
  an existing config.
- If you installed v1.0.0/v1.1.0 with the old `raw.githubusercontent.com` bootstrapping URL,
  switch to the release-pinned command above: it resolves a real tag and verifies checksums.
- The CI upgrade-path job proves a v1.1.0-era config loads, normalizes and validates under the
  new binary, and that a wizard re-run merges over it instead of dropping operator keys.

## Checksums

Every artifact in this release is covered by `SHA256SUMS`. Download it from the release and run
`sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing` before installing.

releases.name: TeleMeetBot v1.1.0
releases.body:
# TeleMeetBot v1.1.0 — presenting that actually works

**A reliability release for the two things that broke in real meetings: Meet refusing to start the
share, and YouTube showing a consent wall or green frames instead of the clip.**

This is a minor bump over v1.0.0 because it adds two diagnostic entry points (`--probe`,
`--media-probe`) and a new consent-handling module. No configuration key was removed or renamed.

## Why upgrade

v1.0.0 could join a meeting and click Present, but three failures were reproducibly fatal:

1. **“Presentation is starting…” forever.** Chromium's auto-select capture matches the
   browser-side tab title. The old title lock used a getter with a no-op setter, so the native
   title never changed and no tab matched. Headless Chromium has no picker to fall back on.
2. **Participants saw “Before you continue to YouTube”** instead of the video: the media tab was
   shared while the consent lightbox owned the page. The old matcher required an exact
   `reject all` label, and real buttons carry full sentences in the visitor's language.
3. **Green or black frames.** Fake media devices plus a software renderer without the right flags
   produced uninitialised YUV buffers, and nothing verified that the shared surface was painting.

All three are fixed and covered by tests that use a real Chromium and a real `getDisplayMedia`
grant, not mocks.

## Highlights

### Presenting

- **Leaf-button matcher** for Meet's Present control: the toolbar container is skipped, so the
  click lands on the actual button.
- **Real tab title.** The player document is served over loopback and the tab title is set through
  the native setter, so `--auto-select-tab-capture-source-by-title` matches `TeleMeet Media` —
  including the title Meet reports.
- **No fake devices.** `use-fake-device-for-media-stream` and `use-fake-ui-for-media-stream` were
  removed so tab capture shares the real tab; camera and microphone are muted on prejoin instead.
- **No present-menu reopen loop.** A failed menu open now dumps the menu DOM and fails with a
  diagnosable error instead of re-clicking in a loop.
- **Survives CDP hiccups.** A transient protocol error no longer kills a live stream.

### Consent and playback

- New `internal/engine/consent.go`: structural detection (consent hosts, DOM markers in light DOM
  *and* shadow roots, visible-only heuristics, text hints), locale phrase tables with reject
  preferred over accept, blocked decoys (`Customize`, `More options`, `Learn more`), one
  normalisation path for both sides (NFD, all combining marks dropped — required for kana),
  and a click ladder: JS → physical mouse → keyboard, then the other action family.
- The wall is also dismissed **after** the watch page reports a buffered video, because YouTube
  mounts it a few seconds late.
- Playback is now *verified*, not assumed: position must advance and sampled pixels must be
  neither black nor decoder-green. The report carries the surface, the URL and the attempt list.
- `recoverMedia` repairs a tab (consent → refit → replay) **without** re-clicking Share Screen:
  the capture track is bound to that tab.
- The watch loop self-heals a consent wall, a stall or a black surface every 10 s, bounded to five
  attempts, and only re-presents after two consecutive misses.

### Networking

- Media traffic can use a proxy (`browser.proxy`, e.g. SOCKS5) while Google Meet traffic bypasses
  it, so WebRTC latency is unaffected and datacenter bot checks apply only to media hosts.
- Headless rendering uses `--headless=new` with SwiftShader ANGLE flags to avoid green frames.

### Joining

- **Host-gated lobbies are waitable.** “No one can join unless invited or admitted by the host”
  keeps the session in `admitting` and re-requests entry every 30 s until
  `meet.admit_wait_seconds` expires. Meeting-full, ended and invalid-code screens still fail fast.
- Debug-grade telemetry: stage, elapsed time and attempt count while gated; explicit joined and
  stream-live milestones; `[STEP n/6]` pipeline logs.

### Diagnostics

- `telemeetbot --probe <meet-url> [--probe-media <url>] [--probe-seconds N]` runs one live session
  through the real engine, streams every stage to the log, serves `/livez` for the window and exits
  without touching Telegram.
- `telemeetbot --media-probe <url>` plays a link in the same player and reports consent state,
  viewport, `overlayFree`, `readyState`, position advance, mean RGB, a verification verdict and a
  human-readable failure. No meeting required.
- The doctor now accepts a health port already served by a live TeleMeetBot instead of reporting a
  conflict.

### Fixes

- Probe event-draining goroutine deadlock on session end.
- `scripts/install.sh`: SIGPIPE on the latest-release lookup, and checksum lines prefixed with
  `./` are handled.
- `scripts/release.sh` writes bare archive names into `SHA256SUMS`.
- Corrected the Docker first-run command in `README.md`, `README.fa.md` and `docker-compose.yml`:
  the compose entrypoint is `tini`, so the binary name is required —
  `docker compose run --rm telemeetbot telemeetbot --wizard --config /data/telemeetbot.yml`.

## New documentation site

`website/` builds a static Astro site (search, dark and light themes, mobile-first layout) that
generates its facts from the Go source at build time: CLI flags, bot commands, config keys, states,
health fields, media extensions, test counts and release targets. Enabled by default:
`https://opselon.github.io/TeleMeetBot-TeleMeetBot-implementation/`.

## Upgrade

Archives are attached below with `SHA256SUMS`. No config migration is needed.

```bash
VERSION=v1.1.0
curl -fsSLO "https://github.com/Opselon/TeleMeetBot-TeleMeetBot-implementation/releases/download/$VERSION/telemeetbot-linux-amd64.tar.gz"
curl -fsSLO "https://github.com/Opselon/TeleMeetBot-TeleMeetBot-implementation/releases/download/$VERSION/SHA256SUMS"
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing
tar -xzf telemeetbot-linux-amd64.tar.gz
sudo install -m 0755 telemeetbot /usr/local/bin/telemeetbot
sudo systemctl restart telemeetbot
```

Docker:

```bash
git pull
docker compose build
docker compose up -d
```

Then verify the real capture path on the host, not just the version string:

```bash
telemeetbot --config /etc/telemeetbot/config.yml --check --capture-test
telemeetbot --config /etc/telemeetbot/config.yml --media-probe "<a link you use>" --probe-seconds 15
```

## Behaviour changes to know about

- A host-gated lobby now waits instead of failing on the first restrictive screen. If nobody admits
  the bot, the error arrives after `meet.admit_wait_seconds` (default 5 minutes; `0` waits forever) with both likely
  causes named.
- The bot refuses to present a tab whose consent wall will not clear, and says which controls it
  tried. That is a hard failure by design: presenting the wall is worse than not presenting.
- Media hosts may now resolve through `browser.proxy`; Meet hosts always connect directly.

## Tests

- `go test ./...` — 53 unit tests across config, bot, engine, store, setup, web, health.
- `go test ./internal/engine -run TestIntegration` — 13 real-Chromium tests, including 16 consent
  variants across 13 locales (text-only, shadow DOM, no accept button, no wall, inert wall) and an
  end-to-end case where the wall mounts *after* the share is live and the same capture track keeps
  delivering non-black frames.
- Opt-in live checks (`TELEMEETBOT_YOUTUBE_URL`, `TELEMEETBOT_PROXY`) are never required by CI.
- CI runs gofmt, `go vet`, the unit suite, the Chromium integration suite, a Docker build, and the
  website build with its SEO, contrast and Playwright audits.

## Known limitations

- Guest join only; meetings that require a Google sign-in cannot be joined.
- Meet's UI must be English (`browser.lang: en-US`).
- One presenter per session; two sessions in one meeting compete for the role.
- `media.autoplay`, `media.loop` and `telegram.notify_chat_id` are parsed but not read. Playback
  starts after the share is confirmed, the player always loops, notifications go to the launching
  chat.
- No control API: `/healthz` and `/livez` are read-only, and control is Telegram-only.
- Playback still depends on the source: pages that require a login, block framing or refuse
  automated browsers will not play, and there is no credential injection.

## Changes since v1.0.0

- #1 host gate waitable, `--probe`, richer logging
- #2 YouTube green screen, proxy routing, step logs, media probe
- #3 real capture tab title
- #4 consent wall dismissal and verified playback

Full commit list: `git log v1.0.0..v1.1.0 --oneline`.

releases.name: TeleMeetBot v1.0.0
releases.body:
# TeleMeetBot v1.0.0 — first release

**The first public release: a 100% Go, headless Google Meet streaming bot with a Telegram dashboard.**

## Highlights

* Headless Chromium streaming engine driven by rod/CDP:
  `--enable-usermedia-screen-capturing`,
  `--auto-select-desktop-capture-source=…`, autoplay permitted, stock Chrome UA override.
* Real guest-flow automation in Google Meet: guest name → join → Present now → tab capture.
* Telegram dashboard: home, sessions, settings, health + live session cards
  (pause/resume, mute/unmute, volume ±, seek ±10 s, restart, stop, refresh).
* 2-minute setup wizard (`telemeetbot --wizard`), doctor (`--check`) and a real
  getDisplayMedia capture self-test (`--check --capture-test`).
* Per-session isolation, strict fail-closed admin allow-list, first-start admin claim.
* Operation ready: Dockerfile + compose (1 GiB shm, healthcheck), systemd unit,
  one-command installer, cross-arch release archives:
  linux/amd64 · linux/arm64 · linux/armv6 · linux/armv7 · linux/386.
* Surfaces of note: only `/healthz` + `/livez` are exposed (no remote control HTTP).
* Tests: unit suites for config/wizard/bot/store/web plus real-Chromium integration
  tests, also running in CI with `browser-actions/setup-chrome`.

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Opselon/TeleMeetBot-TeleMeetBot-implementation/main/scripts/install.sh | bash
```

or Docker:

```bash
docker compose run --rm telemeetbot --wizard --config /data/telemeetbot.yml
docker compose up -d
```

SHA256 checksums for the archives are attached below (`SHA256SUMS`).
